text: Stop keeping big money in your savings account. Your bank earns three times more on it.
Here is your town. You put one lakh rupees in your SBI savings account.
The bank pays you two point five percent. That is two thousand five hundred rupees a year.
So where does the rest of your money go?
The bank lends it to a home buyer, at seven point five percent or more. That is seven thousand five hundred rupees a year, back to the bank.
The gap is about five thousand rupees a year on your one lakh. Simplified, because banks also pay for staff, branches, reserves and bad loans.
What can you do? Keep three to six months of expenses in savings. For the rest, compare a sweep-in FD or a liquid fund.
Follow for more money truths. And stop keeping big money in your savings account.
